correctness.rationale: For square incidence matrix A, AA^T=A^TA=(k-lambda)I+lambda J, and symmetric design identity v*lambda=k*(k-1)+lambda. Inverting the bipartite Laplacian on two zero-mean blocks, then restoring its one anti-constant eigenvector, yields the exact transfer-current kernel P_ef=[k(delta_p,pprime+delta_l,lprime)-A_p,lprime-A_pprime,l]/(v lambda)+1/(vk). The five row classes sum to vk edges, and the crossed-incidence classes alone carry negative entries. Since P 1=1, absolute row sums yield exact ||P||_inf. Q=I-P differs only at the diagonal, yielding ||Q||-||P||=(k-4)/k+2/(vk). Sign input vectors attain norms. Fresh independent pinned-Laplacian solve on Fano incidence graph recovers each transfer entry and norm; finite test not a universal proof.
